sourceDesign.provenanceNote: Eighteen D1 frames (notification detail, level review history, platform queue, platform detail with approve and deny confirmations; light and dark) exported read-only at scale 1 and committed unchanged. They were designed after D1 left these surfaces blocked and were approved by the issue owner. The sourceDesign digest tracks the pen as it was when the frames were exported; a later pen edit by another unit does not invalidate the pinned PNGs, which are pinned by their own digests.

routes.NotificationDetailPage: /notifications/$notificationId (the community invitation branch keeps its approved U8 frames and is unchanged)

stateMapping: All 18 frames have an app counterpart; none is frame-only. Unread / read map to the real mark-read result (unread until the server confirms, read after). Approve / deny with note map to the AlertDialog confirmations of the real decision flow.

frameOnlyElements.previousLevel: d0Qcrm / U3UJJj draw a Previous level row (3.51). The notification context carries only the requested range, the approved level, the decision date and the note, so the card shows Requested range, Updated level and Decided (D6: no invented data).
frameOnlyElements.winChipAndTeams: dkFFb / k2CxJR draw a viewer-relative Win chip, both pairs with set scores and a Level 3.76 to 3.82 / +0.06 rating-change line. The result notification context carries the classification, the winner and loser set counts, the score string, the group and version, the submitter and the deadline, so the card shows the real outcome chip (classification) and those facts (D6: outcome data from the real classification only). The rating change is not in the context and is not shown.
frameOnlyElements.queueCommunity: SCPeI draws the player community under the name. The queue row carries no community; the real submitted level and reliability take that slot.
frameOnlyElements.historyStatusLine: A9f626 draws Awaiting a decision. for the pending card. The card shows the real status detail copy (Waiting for Platform Admin review.) and, for decided requests, the real decision note.
frameOnlyElements.detailCurrentRange: Y7NRH draws Current level range 3.25 to 3.50 and a community line. The request snapshot carries one level and a reliability percentage, shown as Level when submitted; there is no community on the request.
frameOnlyElements.inlineApproval: e8Z3Rb / rBhs4 draw the approval or denial preview inline with a sticky Cancel / Confirm bar. The app keeps the modal AlertDialog (focus trap, restore, stale-rating guard, retry with the same command); the sheet shows the real server preview (level after approval, reliability) and the entered note. A frame-only nuance: the unchanged-reliability tag appears only when the preview shows no reliability change.
frameOnlyElements.levelReviewNewRequest: A9f626 has no request-level-review action. The request link stays under the intro when the player has no active request (behavior preserved).

intentionalDifferences: History, queue and detail keep the title next to the back target (shared with the request and status headers); the notification detail centers the title like the frame.
The type tile and chip glyphs are text glyphs (decorative, aria-hidden) instead of the frame icon set; the label always carries the meaning.
Received time is shown in UTC with a UTC suffix, matching the notification feed; the frame sample is local time.
Deny replaces Reject and Denied replaces Rejected on the level review surfaces in en, pt-BR and es to match the frames.
The status filter, the load-more actions, the empty states and the load error states of the history and queue are kept; the frames draw only populated lists.

visualBudgets.measurementMethod: Chromium 390 CSS px (viewport 390x800), deviceScaleFactor 1, en, Figtree 400-800 loaded, service worker blocked. Each live region is clipped from a full-page capture (viewport capture for the sticky bar and the confirmation sheet, where the element is pinned) at the top of the aligned element and compared with the same-size region of the scale-1 Pencil PNG (frame y = live y + 44: the status bar is device chrome) with the pinned perceptual threshold (35215 x 0.1^2). Structural probes (type sizes and weights, 48px back target at x8, 44/52px avatars and tiles, 20px card radius with hairline, 14px card step, 52px actions, 108px Deny/Cancel, sticky bar insets, no overflow at 320 and 1280, 44px targets) assert exactly and are independent of the budgets.
